blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Percent-encoded e-mail addresses reach the logs in full) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The pattern only matches a literal `@`. A message or field holding a URL or query string — `logInfo("GET /reset?email=ada.lovelace%40example.org")` — has no `@`, so `maskEmails` returns it unchanged and the full address is written to the hosting provider's logs, kept 90 days (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and Art. 32). Also match the encoded separator (`%40`, case-insensitive) — or decode before matching — and add a test with an encoded address.
findings.title: Percent-encoded e-mail addresses reach the logs in full

findings.recommendation: The local part and the domain accept only `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]` and `[A-Za-z0-9.-]`. `andré@example.org` (accented local part) and `ada@exämple.fr` (internationalised domain) do not match at all and are logged in full; `jean.o'neil@example.org` matches only from `neil`, giving `jean.o'n***@example.org`, which keeps most of the person's name. The proposal promises to mask "every e-mail address". Widen the classes to the characters RFC 5322/6531 allow (for instance `[^\s@<>()"]` for the local part and `[\p{L}\p{N}.-]` with the `u` flag for the domain), and cover these cases in `src/logger.test.ts`.
findings.title: Addresses with characters outside the ASCII class escape masking

findings.recommendation: Only values go through `maskEmails`; keys are copied as is. A caller logging a map keyed by address — `logInfo("quota", { "ada@example.org": 3 })` — writes the full address to the logs. Whether any caller does depends on code not in this change. Mask the key too (`safe[maskEmails(key)] = …`).
findings.title: Field keys are written to the log without masking

findings.recommendation: `a***@example.org` keeps the whole domain and the first letter. For a customer on a personal or small company domain (`a***@lovelace-family.fr`), the masked value still points to one person, so the log stays personal data (GDPR Art. 4(1), Art. 5(1)(c)). Depends on the customer base, which the review cannot see. If the domain is not needed for diagnosis, replace the address with a fixed token or a keyed hash.
findings.title: The kept domain and first letter may re-identify a customer
